home.description: Four seats face a field of 192 squares. Place your reserve pieces, find a route through the gates, and work with the player across the board.
home.boardLabel: Four corner forts, one shared board
home.ruleTitle: A different kind of four-player chess
home.ruleBody: Red and White share a team. Blue and Black share the other. A player who is checkmated leaves the game, but their partner can keep fighting.
home.sourceNote: This is an independently authored reconstruction of the Russian rules described by Alexander Petrov. A few unresolved endings are identified in the tutorial.

welcome.title: Four seats, one board
welcome.body: This version follows Alexander Petrov's Russian four-player description. It is an independent reconstruction; it does not reproduce historical board art or text.

board.title: Read the 192 squares
board.body: The board is a 12-by-12 central field joined to four corner fortresses. Each fort has two short walls and a gate route. A move cannot cross a wall or cut diagonally around a wall end.

teams.title: Find your partner
teams.body: Turns move clockwise: Red at the top, Blue at the right, White at the bottom, then Black at the left. Red and White are partners; Blue and Black are partners.

reserve.title: Place your reserve
reserve.body: Each player places an extra bishop, knight and rook in distinct squares of the fortress on their right. Red begins. Select the bishop, then place it at a13.

turns.title: Pawns face inward
turns.body: Each seat moves its pawns toward the centre. A pawn may advance two squares on its first move when both are clear. Red's pawn can move from e13 to e11; then Blue gets a turn.

pieces.title: Use ordinary chess moves
pieces.body: Rooks follow ranks and files; bishops follow diagonals; queens combine them. Kings step one square. Knights take one orthogonal step and one diagonal step in either order, while jumping pieces but respecting walls.

walls.title: A wall blocks every route
walls.body: The raised wall is part of the rules. For example, a bishop cannot take the diagonal from n2 to m3, and cannot cut past the ends at n4–m5 or m4–n5. A gate is the open route around the inner wall.

enPassant.title: Capture the two-square move
enPassant.body: A pawn may capture en passant only on the very next seat's turn after an opposing pawn advances two squares. Blue's pawn on f11 can take Red's pawn on e11 by moving to e12.

castling.title: Castle along your rank
castling.body: The king moves two squares toward an unmoved rook and the rook crosses to the square beside it. The route must be clear, avoid walls, and keep the king out of check along the way.

promotion.title: Promote on a home rank
promotion.body: A pawn that reaches an ordinary home rank of another seat promotes to a queen, rook, bishop or knight. Promotion inside a fortress is left out because the surviving descriptions do not settle it.

checkmate.title: Checkmate removes a seat
checkmate.body: A move must keep its own king safe; it does not have to protect its partner's king. At the start of a turn, a checked player with no escape is checkmated and all of their pieces leave the board. A team wins after both opposing seats are gone.

stalemate.title: A safe king with no move
stalemate.body: The historical stalemate outcome is uncertain. This digital edition chooses an immediate draw when a player has no legal move and is not in check. Which result does this edition use?

rules.title: How Fortress Chess works
rules.board: A 192-square board with a central field and four corner forts. Walls block lines and the forbidden diagonal shortcuts around wall ends.
rules.teams: Red and White are allied against Blue and Black. Turns move clockwise from Red.
rules.setup: Place a bishop, knight and rook in distinct cells of your right-hand fortress before ordinary moves begin.
rules.endings: Checkmate removes one seat. A team wins after both opposing seats are removed. This edition treats stalemate as a draw.
rules.source: Petrov's surviving rules are the historical basis. Stalemate, reserve placement and some special-move details are labeled digital choices.
